  CITY OF SANTA MONICA

  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES

  JUNE 10, 2025

  A regular meeting of the Santa Monica City Council was called to order by Mayor Negrete at 5:30 p.m., on

  STATEMENT OF  The City of Santa Monica is located on the land of Tovangaar. With
  ACCOUNTABILITY  great respect, the City acknowledges the Gabrieleño/Tongva as the
  (LAND  First People of this ancestral and unceded territory of Kuruvungna, a
  ACKNOWLEDGEMENT)  village that we know as Santa Monica. We honor their elders, past and
  present, and the Gabrieleño descendants who are part of the
  Gabrieleño /Tongva tribes.

  We recognize that these peoples are still here, and as settlers and
  kuyam (guests), we recognize our responsibility and obligation to care
  for their land in partnership with them. The City of Santa Monica
  commits to work in partnership with the Gabrieleño/Tongva people to
  uplift their voices and visibility on their ancestral land.

  The City of Santa Monica Statement of Accountability (Land
  Acknowledgement) was read into the record by Mayor Pro Tem Torosis.

  SANTA MONICA BLVD  recommendations of the Santa Monica Blvd Safety Study, funded by
  SAFETY STUDY  a Caltrans Sustainable Transportation Planning grant, was presented.

  Recommended Action
  1. Staff recommends that the City Council:
  2. Adopt a finding that this study session is not a “project” subject to
  the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA); and
  3. Receive, discuss, and provide direction regarding the initial
  findings and concept level recommendations for the Santa Monica

  Questions asked and answered of staff included: what are the goals and
  metrics including how the city will track measurable outcomes for safety
  improvements; how will the city prioritize people without vehicles; is the
  department thinking about the potential trade-offs that will need to be made
  to implement the improvements; are there other potential pedestrian/bike
  crossings being considered between 17th Street and Yale around McKinley
  and Park Avenue; why aren’t far siding bus stops being done on 26th Street;
  why is a queue jump not necessary; could the bus lanes exist with the curb
  extensions; what is being done to reduce travel speeds specifically
  addressing the speeds on the eastern side of the corridor on Santa Monica
  Blvd.; how might reducing lane widths and reducing the amount of travel
  lanes on streets like Wilshire, Lincoln, San Vicente, and Santa Monica
  Blvd. impact speed and safety on the corridor and why is that not being
  considered anywhere in this study; what is the relationship between
  multiple lanes and safety on a corridor; is there data on how many
  pedestrians and cyclists have been struck on Wilshire Boulevard since the
  safety improvements were installed; is the city satisfied with the
  improvements that were done on Wilshire Blvd. in terms of pedestrian
  safety; are those same improvements being emulated here on Santa Monica

  HOUSING PROJECTS  Projects, was heard.

  Request of Councilmember Zwick, Mayor Pro Tem Torosis, and
  Mayor Negrete that the City Council direct the City Manager to
  return with a pilot program allowing market-rate housing projects
  more flexibility in how they provide affordable housing units off-site
  as a means to incentivize housing production for approved projects
